query: What signals suggest an agent's tickets will take longer to resolve?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Categorizing incidents (email, vpn, database, etc.) gives a strong grouping axis to compare resolution times across ticket types. Values are sound readings of short_description (e.g. 'Unable to access the database' -> database).

per_column.name: incident_symptom_type
per_column.rationale: Symptom taxonomy (cannot_connect, access_denied, outage_down) is an orthogonal, useful axis for modeling complexity/duration. Extractions from descriptions are mostly warranted, though some readings are debatable (e.g. 'unable to access database' as access_denied).

per_column.name: affected_scope
per_column.rationale: Scope (individual vs organization-wide) is plausibly predictive of resolution effort. However short descriptions rarely state scope; assignments like 'Internet connection unstable' -> organization_wide, or 'Unable to access the database' -> server_system, are confident inferences the text does not clearly support.

per_column.name: service_outage_flag
per_column.rationale: An outage flag is a reasonable severity signal for duration analysis. Values are broadly derivable from wording, though some judgment calls are less certain; samples appear plausible.

per_column.name: remote_access_flag
per_column.rationale: Flags VPN/remote-access tickets, a distinct axis that may correlate with resolution time. Grounded well (VPN issue -> True; database access -> False).

per_column.name: assigned_agent
per_column.rationale: The query is agent-centric, so an agent identifier is relevant; but this largely duplicates the existing assigned_to original column, reducing added leverage. Values match plausibly.

per_column.name: cross_agent_resolution_flag
per_column.rationale: Whether a ticket was handled by multiple agents is highly relevant to resolution delay. But this cannot be derived from the sampled source fields (single short_description + timestamps); no evidence of reassignment history is present, so the true/false values appear largely invented.

per_column.name: ticket_open_status
per_column.rationale: Open vs closed status matters for resolution analysis but is essentially a restatement of the original 'state'/'closed_at' fields, limiting new leverage. Derivable from state/closed_at.

per_column.name: opened_hour_of_day
per_column.rationale: Time-of-day bucket (business/extended/off hours) is a genuine signal for slower resolution and is derivable from opened_at. One sample buckets a 08:34 close, but derivation from opened_at is sound.

per_column.name: opened_day_of_week
per_column.rationale: Weekday vs weekend is a plausible driver of longer resolution and derivable from opened_at timestamp.

judge.rationale: Most added columns provide genuine, orthogonal axes (category, symptom, remote-access, timing) directly relevant to explaining resolution duration for agents, and are largely grounded in short_description and timestamps. Weaknesses: assigned_agent and ticket_open_status mostly restate existing original columns, and affected_scope and especially cross_agent_resolution_flag assert facts (scope, multi-agent handling) not supported by the sampled source text, indicating hallucination.
